items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: He was a kid, you know, along with Michael and what have you.

ctx.x: He was a kid, you know, along with Michael and what have you. I said, "Why don't you just learn how to touch the drums, like your father?" But you must remember, Milt, that the experience coming out of the World War II, they took the dance floor away. They took the big bands away. Now the best the kid could do was sit and play at a corner bar somewhere and take some four bars and play within that framework. The consistency was broken. We've had a consistency broken for the last 22 years and we've had so much…
Berry used to always say they should have major and minor league in music like there is in baseball.
